label: Axes and Units
subgoals: The horizontal axis usually holds the input and the vertical axis the output.
A point is read as an ordered pair.
Graphs can show distance against time, cost against quantity, or any other pair of related quantities.

label: Slope and Intercept
subgoals: The slope describes how fast the output changes per unit of input.
A horizontal segment means the output is not changing.
On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means a faster speed and a flat line means the object is stationary.

label: Interpreting Features
subgoals: Turning points, plateaus and intercepts each have a meaning in context.
The x-intercept is where the output is zero; the y-intercept is the output when the input is zero.
Interpretations must stay within the domain of the graph.
